sources.name: Copernicus DEM public AWS readme.html
sources.version: No explicit edition/version in document; exact response bytes/hash and retrieval date pin this recheck
sources.exact_relevant_text: [resolution] - resolution in arc seconds (not meters!), which is 10 for GLO-30, and 30 for GLO-90.
sources.interpretation: Readme describes filename token Copernicus_DSM_COG_[resolution]_... as resolution in arc seconds and assigns 30 to GLO-90. This conflicts with selected COG header measurement (about 3 arc-seconds); preserve/document the discrepancy, and do not use the filename token as a substitute for physical grid spacing.

sources.name: Selected Copernicus DEM GLO-90 COG header range
sources.method: GDAL gdalinfo -json -noct on the returned TIFF header bytes; no raster cells read.

header_observations.arc_seconds_calculation: 0.0008333333333333 × 3600 = 2.99999999988 arc-seconds; independently, 3600 arc-seconds per degree / 1200 pixels per degree = 3 arc-seconds per pixel.
header_observations.tile_name_token_interpretation: Distribution filename component; do not restate as the measured physical pixel spacing for this COG.

methods: Retrieved the exact public README URL and compared full response size/SHA-256 to the earlier source manifest; inspected its filename convention wording.
Fetched the first 8192 bytes of the already identified public COG using a byte range and ran GDAL header inspection; no full raster or pixel values used.
Calculated angular grid spacing from the header increment and independently from 3600 arc-seconds per degree divided by 1200 pixels per degree.
